top_signals.title: China Turns to Iraqi Oil as U.S. Blockade Chokes Iranian Supply
top_signals.summary: Chinese independent refiners are seeking crude oil cargoes from Iraq using the services of global commodity trading houses in a departure from their usual oil-sourcing practices, Bloomberg has reported, noting the continued U.S. blockade on Iranian ports. The so-called teapots have for years enjoyed discounted Iranian and Russian crude, but this year, the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran upended supply chains; the U.S. blockade paralyzed Iranian oil exports and Russian crude became more expensive. So, the teapots are buying crude…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: China’s Economy Disappoints With New Stimulus Yet to Kick In
top_signals.summary: China’s growth weakened across the board in October as investment unexpectedly worsened while consumption and industrial output undershot estimates, in a sign Beijing’s latest stimulus measures have yet to feed through to the economy.
